description:
🚫 **A story whose CORRECT answer is `false` makes its tasklist permanently uncompletable, and chief has no way to say so.** Measured on cuneiform `283-nixos-bare-metal-vpn-topology-target`, 2026-08-22 → 2026-08-25.

Its US-3 read *"VERIFY the MaaS commission→deploy flow, honestly"*, and the criterion said in as many words: *"if it does not complete, **THIS STORY STAYS `passes: false`** and the precise failure point is written into `bare-metal.md` — a stubbed phone-home does not count as a pass."* The flow genuinely does not complete: the verdict is `maas-client-absent`, and no file under `core/`, `services/`, `apps/`, `packages/` or `infrastructure/` calls a MaaS API at all. So `passes: false` **was the correct, measured outcome** — the story was DONE and its answer was negative.

**Chief has exactly one notion of done — every story true — so it re-drove the branch forever.** 63 commits. 21 iterations in a single run, 59 across the program, and **42 consecutive IDENTICAL measurements**. The agent never faked it: it tried the stub route, got `1 provisioned` against a 40-line stub it had written for the measurement, and REJECTED its own result because the criterion excluded exactly that. It collapsed its own notes at iteration 32 after they had grown to ~44 KB of duplicate text, and its terminal note read: *"criterion 1 makes `passes: false` the CORRECT end state, so this tasklist can NEVER report all-stories-true and no further iteration can change that. It needs MANUAL RETIREMENT."* It was right, it said so in the only channel it had, and nothing could hear it.

**`112` does not cover this and neither does `111`.** `112` fixes progress DETECTION — a bookkeeping commit no longer scores as progress. `111` fixes an iteration that never reached the model. Both are about whether an iteration counted. **This is about whether the tasklist is DONE**, and with both of those fixed `283` would still have run out its budget and been marked INCOMPLETE, which is a wrong verdict on finished work rather than a cheaper wrong verdict.

**The shape recurs.** talos `80` hit the same wall from the other side — its AC1 conflated wiring the lane (delivered) with executing it (blocked on another repo), and was re-passed eight times across 18 iterations before being split. A negative finding is a legitimate deliverable, and the tasklist format currently cannot express one.

userStories.title: A story can declare that FALSE is its terminal answer
userStories.description: The missing vocabulary. A verification story whose honest result is negative has delivered its work, and the format must be able to say that.
acceptanceCriteria: A story may declare that a negative result is TERMINAL — an explicit field on the story, never inferred from prose and never a magic value in `notes`. A story carrying it and answering false is COMPLETE for the purposes of tasklist completion, while its `passes` flag stays false because the answer really is false

The recorded answer and the finding are BOTH preserved and distinguishable: a reader (and `chief ps`) can tell 'this story is done and the answer is no' from 'this story is not done yet'. Collapsing them is the defect — `283` rendered as unfinished work for three days

The declaration is INERT unless the story also carries evidence of the attempt. A terminal-false story that recorded no measurement is not done, it is skipped, and the two must not be spellable the same way — otherwise this becomes a way to mark hard stories complete
Nothing changes for a story without the declaration: it completes only by passing, exactly as today. Asserted over the existing tasklist corpus, which must classify identically before and after
userStories.notes: test/terminal-false.sh: PASS — a declared negative settles, survives into completed/, is never re-driven; an undeclared story untouched; an unmeasured declaration settles nothing. Corpus assertion green: 40 existing tasklists classify identically before and after. Gates: bash -n clean over bin/chief + engine/*.sh + test/*.sh + install.sh; smoke PASS, ratelimit PASS, noworkguard PASS, measured-bars PASS, evidence-gate PASS; version-bump PASS (VERSION 0.8.98 covers every engine/bin change on HEAD); doc-sync PASS (README states v0.8.98). shellcheck not installed on this host — CI enforces it.

userStories.title: A tasklist that cannot complete is DETECTED and stops, rather than running to the cap
userStories.description: The safety net for the case where nobody remembered to declare it. 283 was diagnosable from its own record by iteration 6.
acceptanceCriteria: When a story's recorded outcome is IDENTICAL across N consecutive iterations — same measurement, same blocker, no change to `passes` — the run STOPS and reports that the tasklist appears unable to complete, naming the story and quoting the repeated finding. `283` produced 42 identical measurements; the signal was available long before that

The report names the two actions that resolve it — amend the criterion, or declare the negative terminal (US-1) — because 'it stalled' sent an operator to re-scope a tasklist whose work was intact and whose agent had already written the correct diagnosis

This fires INDEPENDENTLY of the progress counter, since the failure mode is a story that is legitimately being re-measured rather than an agent doing nothing. It must catch `283` even with `112`'s bookkeeping fix in place, and a test asserts exactly that

N is configurable with a stated default, and the comparison is on the story's recorded outcome rather than on commit count — `283` produced a commit every iteration and each one was real, just not new

userStories.title: The operator can retire a tasklist on a negative without hand-editing JSON
userStories.description: 283's agent asked for MANUAL RETIREMENT in its notes. There is no command for that, so the ask had nowhere to land.
acceptanceCriteria: A command retires a tasklist whose delivered stories passed and whose remaining story terminated false — filing the `completed/` record, recording WHICH story terminated negative and its finding, and stopping the tasklist being re-driven

It REFUSES a tasklist whose stories are merely unfinished. The distinction is the whole point: `283` had two passing stories and one measured negative, which is not the same as a tasklist that stopped halfway, and a command that cannot tell them apart is a way to bury incomplete work

The `completed/` record carries the negative finding in a form a successor tasklist can cite. A story that terminates false often names the thing to do instead — that closing action is the most valuable output of the whole tasklist, and it must survive in the record rather than only in a run log, so whoever authors the successor can point at it.

Mutation-check it: a tasklist with an ordinary unfinished story is refused; one with a declared terminal-false story is retired; a tasklist with NO evidence on the terminal-false story is refused. A retirement path that cannot be shown to refuse is a way to lose work
